title: refactor(ci): modernize workflows, bump actions/deps, and improve cache/matrix hygiene
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Modernized CI workflows: split lint/test/release flows, upgraded actions and Node versions, improved caching and reduced build matrix size to speed CI and reduce flakes.
description: Summary: Modernize and clean up GitHub Actions workflows across the monorepo to reduce CI flakiness, speed up common paths, and make release automation more robust. Motivation: Over time workflows accumulated duplicated steps, an oversized matrix, and outdated third-party actions leading to long queue times and intermittent cache misses. This PR consolidates common steps, splits responsibilities (lint/test/release), upgrades Node and GitHub Action versions, improves cache keys, and simplifies the release automation path to make rollbacks and debug easier. Changes: - Split monolithic ci.yml into lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml; each workflow is focused and triggers on narrow event sets; - Upgrade Node from 18 -> 20 in build/test workflows and update matrix defaults; - Bump key actions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4) and replace deprecated action usages; - Introduce normalized cache keys with partial fingerprints to reduce busts for transient lockfile changes; - Reduce test matrix by moving slow integration tests to weekly 'perf-canary' pipeline and adding a small fast-integration matrix for PR validation; - Add a shared workflow template for packaging/build steps used by SDKs to prevent drift (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-go, redwood-sdk-typescript); - Replace semantic-release nightly hooks with a guarded release-automation workflow that requires explicit label and passes for changelog generation; - Add a hygiene job that runs monthly to bump GitHub Actions and important build deps automatically and opens a PR when human review is required. Commits summary: - 5 commits: initial split + workflow templates; bump actions and node; cache/key fixes and matrix pruning; release automation adjustments; docs update (CONTRIBUTING.md CI section). Files touched (high level): - .github/workflows/{ci.yml -> lint.yml,test.yml,release.yml,hygiene.yml}; - .github/workflows/.templates/build-template.yml; - scripts/ci/cache-key-gen.sh (small helper); - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md (CI docs); - redwood-sdk-*/workflow YAMLs updated to use shared template. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and update triggers - [x] Upgrade Node and actions - [x] Normalize cache keys and add cache helper - [x] Reduce matrix size and move slow jobs to perf-canary - [x] Add shared build template for SDKs - [x] Update docs and README references - [x] Add tests for workflow linter/validator Why this is safe: All workflow changes are additive or conservative: lint/test work independently, release requires explicit label and passing checks; shared template is backward compatible and SDK repositories were updated to reference the new template. Rollback plan: revert workflow commits (single squash commit) to restore previous CI until followups land. Review conversation (high level): - Diego: "Can we make cache keys more resilient to yarn.lock churn?" Author: "Yes — added partial fingerprinting and a small helper script to compute stable keys; comment included." - Maya: "Moving integrations out of PR CI is a risk for regressions." Author: "Added a fast-integration matrix for critical paths and kept weekly canary runs for full integration coverage; also documented expected signal in docs." - Jonah: "Release change looks good, but ensure tags and changelog generation are covered." Author: "Release workflow now requires changelog job to pass and a release label; added extra validations and unit tests for the changelog step." CI details and history: - First run: lint failed due to deprecated action usage; fixed in second commit and reran. - Second run: tests passed with warnings; cache misses observed and addressed with normalized keys. - Final run: all checks passed. Checks: "lint (ubuntu-latest)": pass; "unit tests (matrix: node20)": pass; "sdk template validation": pass; "release-dryrun": pass. Why this improves developer experience: Faster PR feedback loops due to smaller matrices and better cache hits; easier debugging due to focused workflows and shared templates; predictable release automation path reduces accidental releases and simplifies auditing. Related: ENG-4821 (CI flakiness reduction), ENG-5030 (release automation hygiene), SUP-3142 (customer-reported flaky builds). Files changed count and diff size are intentionally moderate to keep change reviewable. Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from reviewers Diego Rivera and Maya Patel and CI green. Follow-ups: - Monitor canary weekly runs for 2 cycles and adjust matrix as needed - Open follow-up to migrate any remaining repo-specific jobs to the shared template (tracked ENG-5099) - Add metrics dashboard for CI queue time and cache hit ratio (tracked ENG-5101)
